findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are hard-coded in plaintext in the Lambda environment variables, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with read access to the Terraform state, source code, or Lambda console/API. This also matches a well-known AWS example key pattern, but even non-example real credentials embedded this way constitute CWE-798.

The Lambda function does not configure a customer-managed KMS key (kms_key_arn) for encrypting environment variables at rest, relying only on the default AWS-managed key, which reduces control over encryption and key rotation for sensitive data stored in the environment block.
The function uses nodejs12.x, which is an end-of-life/deprecated Lambda runtime no longer receiving security patches, increasing exposure to unpatched vulnerabilities.
